title: Shift Smoky Chilli Turkey Sunday-Style Roast
method: Use unseasoned mince made from 100% skinless turkey breast, weighed raw. Commercial mixed-cut turkey mince is not the specified ingredient; ask the butcher for breast mince or mince skinless breast at home.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Peel the potatoes and weigh the listed raw portion before cutting into even 3cm chunks. Parboil in water for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake gently to roughen the edges. Toss with half the measured olive oil and roast on a non-stick tray for 35–40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender. Time the other components to finish alongside the potatoes.

Cut the carrots into slim batons, toss them with one quarter of the measured olive oil and roast on the potato tray for the final 20–25 minutes, turning once, until tender. Keep them separate from uncooked meat or fish.

Use the final quarter of the measured olive oil on the separate protein tray. Shape the turkey breast mince into two compact, flattened portions about 2cm thick; this uses mince, not a roasting joint. Bake on a separate lined tray for approximately 18–22 minutes, turning halfway, until steaming hot through the centre. Check 75°C for 30 seconds with a clean thermometer.
Cut the broccoli into small florets and boil for 4–6 minutes until tender with a little bite. Drain well.
Warm the smoked chilli tomato sauce in a small saucepan with 2 tablespoons of water for 1–2 minutes, stirring until hot.
Serve the cooked turkey breast mince, roast potatoes, carrots and broccoli together. Spoon the hot smoked chilli tomato sauce over the cooked protein.

title: Shift Creamy Cheddar Chicken Loaded Jacket Potato
method: Scrub the baking potato and pierce it several times with a fork. For an oven, heat to 200°C (180°C fan), put the potato on a tray and bake for about 60–75 minutes. Wash and dry the mixed salad and spring onion. Trim and slice the spring onion very finely, then mix it with the salad to serve alongside the potato.
Use chilled, already-cooked chicken breast; slice it thinly or shred it into small pieces. Keep it refrigerated until assembly.

Finely grate the measured reduced-fat cheddar. Stir together all the measured 0% Greek yoghurt, light mayonnaise, reduced-fat cheddar and olive oil in a small bowl to make the dressing. Keep it refrigerated until assembly.

Split the cooked potato and fluff the centre with a fork. Add the prepared ready-to-eat filling and the prepared dressing; the filling is served chilled on the hot potato. Serve the full mixed salad and finely sliced spring onion alongside, and eat immediately.

For a packed lunch, cool the cooked potato promptly before covering and refrigerating it; pack the chilled filling, dressing and salad separately. Eat within 24 hours and follow any shorter ingredient use-by date. Reheat the potato once until steaming hot throughout, then add the cold toppings immediately before eating.
